attachments.name: crowd_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Looking after people on the day: Eastfield Community Run Half Marathon, Sunday 24 October 2027

Maria Ostrowski, Race Director, Eastfield Athletics

We expect about 550 people altogether, including 550 runners. We do not expect spectators in any number beyond the runners' own companions.

We hired a radio or two last time for the start team, which proved useful, and we had a short briefing for anyone who turned up early. Feedback from runners has been good, and we have no reports of people being unable to find a way through.

Where people will watch
We've set out three viewing spots with barriers: at the finish by the bandstand, at the turn by Pier Promenade, and at the start by the rowing club. We measured them, and at about two people to the square metre they take around 750 between them, which is more than we expect to come.

How we start the race
We set off in 3 waves, four minutes apart, with runners sorted by the time they expect to run. That thins everyone out before the first corner. The pens close five minutes before each wave goes.

Who's helping
We've got 11 stewards in tabards, about one for every 50 people, with 2 supervisors in charge of sections. Each has a set position on a rota, and all come to a briefing an hour before the start.

Getting everyone away
Runners walk through a one-way funnel after the line, out to the recovery area, and leave by the north gate. Spectators have two marked ways out, and a steward stands at each to keep it clear. We reckon the whole place empties in 25 minutes.

Who's in charge
Maria Ostrowski runs the event from the control point with a radio to every supervisor. They can hold a wave, stop the race, or make an announcement over the speakers to move people along. Supervisors call it in if a pen or viewing spot looks to be getting too full.

attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
EVENT MEDICAL PLAN
Eastfield Community Run Half Marathon, Sunday 24 October 2027
Applicant: Eastfield Athletics
Issue: 2.4

1. Event summary
A half marathon race with 550 runners, starting at 09:00 in the Greenhill area of Port Halden. We are not booking a dedicated ambulance for this race.

2. First aid cover
3 first aid posts will operate, at the start, at the finish and at the course midpoint, staffed by 12 qualified first aiders. Posts are placed so that no part of the course is more than 1.5 km from one. Two cycle responders move along the course with defibrillators.

3. Weather and hydration
Participants are reminded in their pre-race information to dress appropriately for the conditions and to drink plenty of fluids before, during and after the race. Our experienced committee will keep a close eye on the weather in the days leading up to the event.

4. Transfer to hospital
The receiving hospital is Valley Regional Hospital, 18 km from the finish. The transfer route and the pick-up point at the rowing club have been walked with the first aid team. The hospital's emergency department has been told the date and the expected numbers.

5. Communications
Members of the team will have their mobile phones with them, and a list of contact numbers will be circulated in the week before the event. Coverage in the area is generally reported to be good.

6. Clinical lead
The medical lead is Fatima Haddad, a registered paramedic, who is on site from an hour before the start until the last runner is cleared. The lead can have any runner withdrawn on medical grounds.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
RACE PLAN
Eastfield Community Run Half Marathon | Sunday 24 October 2027
Organiser: Eastfield Athletics
Race director: Maria Ostrowski
Reference: RQ-76013

Overview
The Eastfield Community Run Half Marathon is a half marathon race of 21 km for 550 entrants, based in the Greenhill area of Port Halden. The start is at 09:00 and the course closes at 12:30.

Course
The course stays entirely on the Saltmarsh Boardwalk and the Pier Promenade, away from the highway, and no road is closed for the race. The finish is at the bandstand.

Course dimensions
The Saltmarsh Boardwalk is a surfaced path about 2.5 m wide, with a railing on one side and a retaining wall on the other. The Pier Promenade section is about 2 m wide and passes under two low bridges. Runners can go two or three abreast at most, and the start pens have to be strung along the path.

Support
Entrants collect numbers from the rowing club from one hour before the start. Timing is by chip, with mats at the start and finish. Results are posted on the Eastfield website the same day.
